clue.text: An encouraging boost when adult gets wounded above the hand?

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
someone wounded above the hand has been hit by a bullet in the limb between wrist and shoulder

explanation.surface: A grown-up gets hurt in the arm, which is somehow supposed to be encouraging.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'An encouraging boost' takes its 'An' as part of the phrase; the wordplay gives a separate A from 'adult', then the phrase for being hit in the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an injection of vigour or encouragement, from a hypodermic jab.

clue.text: Where chessmen move without exception

explanation.surface: Chess pieces travel over the squares without exception.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces literally travel over the playing surface, and the idiom means applying to everyone equally.

clue.text: Wild beast in Augustine's home

explanation.surface: A wild animal lives in the saint's house.
explanation.walkthrough: St Augustine was Bishop of Hippo, an ancient city in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form of hippopotamus, a large African animal; also the Roman North African city where Augustine was bishop.

clue.text: Solid figures posing terrible threat getting read about

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of threat are knocked into a new arrangement
about here means the letters of read are turned around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Geometric shapes pose a dreadful threat to anyone reading about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges THREAT to TETRAH and 'about' rearranges READ to EDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a geometry term for a solid bounded by four triangular faces.

clue.text: VIP engaging British and the French in swindles

indicators.note: engaging means holding or taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: nobs are upper-class or important people, a VIP type taken in the plural
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: An important person involving a Briton and the French in cons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' means the British and French pieces are held inside; a VIP singular stands for the plural toffs here, and 'swindles' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to nobble is to cheat or tamper with, as with a racehorse.

clue.text: Gardener after work may have this dance

definitions.text: Gardener after work may have this dance

parts.words: Gardener after work may have this dance
parts.note: a gardener finishing work would lay the weeding tool on the ground, and that phrase names a lively country dance

explanation.surface: A gardener knocks off work and goes dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American folk dance or the party at which such dancing happens.

clue.text: Song brilliant artist sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the whole sequence is read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the figure 1 looking like I
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A great painter's song gets mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns AIRA (AI for A1, plus RA) upwards; 'sent up' also looks like mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo piece for one voice.

clue.text: Today's paintings could make you shake and tremor!

indicators.note: shake tells you to jumble the letters of the words and tremor

explanation.surface: Contemporary works could leave you shaking and trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective term for contemporary or twentieth-century painting and sculpture.

clue.text: Heeding lesson, I would be silly to show obduracy

indicators.note: silly signals that the letters before it are put into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Heeding a lesson, I'd be foolish to stay stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to refuse stubbornly to change position, like a mule planting its feet.

clue.text: Trustworthy material presented to university panel

parts.note: rep is a ribbed woven fabric
a table can be a board or committee, a panel of people

explanation.surface: Reliable fabric given to a university committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having a good reputation, hence dependable.

clue.text: Lemur visible through thin drizzle

indicators.note: visible through suggests letters showing inside the words thin drizzle

explanation.surface: A lemur glimpsed through a light drizzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest living Madagascan lemur species.

clue.text: Opening a bodily part puts little children off

indicators.note: off means the named letters are removed from the body part

parts.note: the stomach is a digestive organ
CH is a standard abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A part of the body puts small kids off their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes CH from STOMACH, leaving STOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Biology: a mouth-like pore or surgically made aperture in the body.

clue.text: Money henchman brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the henchman is read backwards

parts.note: a tool is a person used by another, a lackey

explanation.surface: A gangster's sidekick returned with the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash, from plunder or stolen goods.

clue.text: Wise men perhaps among patriots

indicators.note: among signals the letters are found inside the word patriots

explanation.surface: Wise men are found among patriots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi traditionally number three, making a threesome.

clue.text: Fantastic actor, titan with pulling power

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild, so the letters of actor and titan are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marvellous actor, a giant with real charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the force or appeal that draws people in.

clue.text: Hair covering two-thirds of big female beast

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: two-thirds of a three-letter word is two letters, here losing the first one

explanation.surface: Hair covers most of a large female animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of' drops the first letter of the three-letter word, and 'covering' has the hair wrap round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the big striped Asian cat.

clue.text: Money invested in plant for producing chemical element

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: the geranium is a flowering garden plant

explanation.surface: Cash is put into a factory to make an element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey metalloid used in semiconductors, number 32 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Salt in treat specially cooked

indicators.note: specially cooked suggests the letters of in treat are prepared in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A salty ingredient in a specially prepared treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: a salt of nitric acid, used in fertilisers and food curing.

clue.text: A murder most foul — one picks up the vibrations

indicators.note: most foul echoes Hamlet, and foul signals that the letters of a murder are mangled

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean 'murder most foul', and someone senses the vibes.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane of the middle ear vibrates in response to sound waves.

clue.text: Expert from west, unconventional sort

parts.note: Mae West was a famous American film actress, so West suggests her first name

indicators.note: unconventional signals that the letters of sort are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An authority from the West turns out to be an odd type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from west' takes MAE from Mae West, the actress; 'unconventional' rearranges SORT to STRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a master of an art, especially a distinguished conductor.

clue.text: The devil improvised

explanation.surface: The devil made it up on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Scratch is a folk name for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old folk name for Satan; also an adjective for something assembled hastily from whatever is at hand, like a scratch team.

clue.text: Nurse has party, very loud celebration for leaver

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade
a do is a party
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A nurse throws a noisy party for someone leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell gathering for someone departing.

clue.text: Sanction given by little old woman

parts.note: O is a short form for old, little indicating the abbreviation
Kay is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Approval granted by a small elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to give approval or permission.

clue.text: Study involving a prominent member of the faculty

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A study that involves a senior academic.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a university faculty or college.

clue.text: Bluebottles heard in cluster of trees

indicators.note: heard means a word spoken aloud gives the letters entered

parts.note: bluebottle is old British slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform

explanation.surface: Buzzing flies heard among a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottles' looks like flies but is slang for police.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thicket or group of trees.

clue.text: Report of freedom from war — but gun is seen

indicators.note: report of means the sound of the following word gives the letters entered

parts.note: peace is the absence of war

explanation.surface: News of a ceasefire, but a gun is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' also suggests a gunshot, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a firearm, especially a handgun.

clue.text: Driver may want to change this outfit

definitions.text: Driver may want to change this

explanation.surface: A motorist may want to change clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's toothed transmission setting which a motorist shifts; also clothing or kit.

clue.text: River about to swamp home behind hospital

indicators.note: to swamp means to engulf, so one piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: behind means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
in means at home

explanation.surface: A river is set to flood the house behind the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts home after hospital, and 'to swamp' has the word for about engulf that pair; 'home' gives IN as in being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A major European waterway flowing from Switzerland to the North Sea.

clue.text: Unreliable lovers watch clock perhaps

explanation.surface: Faithless partners keep checking the time.
explanation.definitionFit: People who cheat on partners; also, read as two words, a pair of time-keeping devices such as a watch and a clock.

clue.text: Memorable dancer though there could be many forgotten

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of many forgotten may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A great dancer, though many are forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed English prima ballerina of the Royal Ballet.
